column4: The financial and legal memoir recounts the author's move into campaigning. Reporting that campaign is not itself an explicit activist declaration; the earlier V5 finding used the broader purpose test. No independent serious V1–V4 finding is established.

V3 remains: the diary's exceptional testimony concerns a particular hidden household and developing inner life; the reviewed evidence still supplies little sustained transferable explanation. Neither revised rule changes that payload finding.

The documented history of missile guidance offers sustained technical and institutional explanation. An anti-nuclear preference does not turn that historical account into an explicit manifesto; the revised expert-narrative allowance also confirms H2 eligibility.

The history explains feedback between overseas bases and war making. Its antiwar conclusion is a political proposal; the earlier record does not establish an explicit activist declaration as the primary work. The revised V5 threshold is not met.

The account of development expertise argues for individual rights through institutional history. Its preferred development policy is an allowed proposal, not sufficient evidence of a manifesto or ideological capture. Prior causal-selection limits remain in the score.

The rent and poverty argument culminates in a land-tax proposal. A normative economic remedy alone does not satisfy revised V5; the sustained causal argument passes H2. Retain the existing limitations on inference rather than invent a new veto.

The graphic argument is explicitly a case for an open-borders political movement and removal of immigration restrictions. Its central mobilizing purpose, rather than graphic form or economic subject, continues to meet V5.

The sustained criticism of historicism and closed political systems is philosophical argument. Its preference for an open society falls within the allowed civilizational inclination; the earlier record does not establish serious V2 or an explicit activist manifesto.

The analysis of data extraction and platform power supports democratic proposals. The earlier veto inferred activism from resistance language without establishing a separate explicit declaration. Allow the analytical work while retaining its existing selection and causal limits.

The account explicitly promotes food sovereignty and collective political action over the food system. The retained evidence describes movement advocacy as a governing aim, beyond merely proposing better agricultural arrangements; V5 remains.

The empirical and philosophical defense of reason, science and progress is an allowed civilizational inclination. It is not automatically an ideological manifesto. Prior doubts about selected progress measures stay in the score; no independent serious veto is established.

The philosophical argument investigates emotions needed by liberal institutions. A preferred political ethic and proposals for civic culture are expressly permitted by revised V5; neither religious doctrine nor an explicit activist declaration is established.

The development and inequality history proposes changes to international institutions. The old decision treated any governing reform program as sufficient; revised V5 does not. Retain the existing causal reservations and thematic deductions.

The work explicitly seeks animal liberation and a change in readers' participation in animal exploitation. This is a declared movement argument, so V5 survives the narrower wording even where ethical reasoning transfers.

The sustained account of pesticide effects and regulatory failures is explanatory nonfiction with policy recommendations. Its influence on environmental activism does not itself make the book an explicit activist declaration; the old broad advocacy finding is insufficient.

The book expressly recruits readers to poverty abolition and collective changes in conduct and policy. This declared civil-activist purpose meets revised V5 independently of the quality of its social research.

The dialogue develops a sustained philosophical inquiry into justice, education and political organization. Its proposed ideal city is an allowed vision; political philosophy alone is not an explicit modern movement manifesto. H1 does not apply to expository dialogue.

The collected political discussions explicitly link their interpretation of power to popular struggle and organized political action. That declared activist purpose supports V5; criticism of American policy by itself would not.

The documented basis is a political indictment of a war and international policy. Such a critical argument is not, without clearer evidence, an explicit manifesto or activist declaration. Existing evidence limits remain; no new V2 is inferred.

The essay expressly argues for feminist and antiwar collective action through changes to education, employment and public institutions. This is a declared political intervention with an activist purpose, not merely incidental social preference.

The historical argument favors cultural renewal through inherited ideals. Revised V5 expressly permits civilizational inclinations and visions; the earlier veto rested on that preference alone. Broad historical inference remains a scoring limitation.

The retained evidence identifies a campaigning political argument for resistance to a named economic program, not only a history with a policy conclusion. That explicit mobilizing purpose sustains V5; it does not establish V1 by itself.

The platform-rent thesis and proposed institutional alternatives constitute an analytical political-economic argument. A vision beyond the present order alone no longer meets V5. The disputed classification and causal weaknesses remain in the score.

A critical case history of foreign interventions is not automatically a manifesto. The earlier evidence establishes an anti-imperialist perspective but not a sufficiently explicit activist declaration; revised V5 permits that inclination. Selection limits remain material.

The lawyer's case narratives and account of punishment offer institutional explanation. A justice-reform preference and the author's activism do not independently establish an explicit manifesto in this memoir. Existing thematic deductions remain.

Natural-history essays develop a land ethic. An environmental moral vision is now expressly allowed unless the work is an explicit activism declaration; the earlier record establishes an ethic, not that stronger category.

The work explicitly organizes its legal history around a reproductive-freedom and racial-justice campaign. The retained evidence supports a central civil-activist declaration, beyond a neutral topic classification, so V5 remains.

The historical indictment is explicitly organized as an emancipatory anti-imperialist ideological argument. That declared political purpose remains V5; the conclusion does not rest merely on Latin American history or criticism of exploitation.

The philosophical case for secular commitment and democratic economic arrangements is a proposed vision. Secular faith is not a religious text merely because of its vocabulary, and the old record does not establish the narrower explicit-activism gate.

V1 remains independently of the revised V5 boundary: the prior reviewed causal argument relies on the exclusive labor basis of surplus and disputed links to prices and profits. The explicit socialist theoretical purpose also remains a V5 ground.

For the identified A Life on Our Planet, the stated organizing purpose is an environmental call to restore the planet through collective action. V5 remains; the historical alternative title Life on Earth must not inherit this identity-dependent finding.

The historical explanation of Islam includes a reformist interpretation. A history of religion and proposed religious reform are not automatically base or derived religious teaching texts; the existing evidence does not establish the narrower V5 category with sufficient clarity.

V4 remains: monetary breakdown and future crisis scenarios carry the central promised payoff. The historical episodes do not validate those forecasts; revised H2 and V5 do not address this independent dependence.
The expository conversations explicitly teach and defend anarchist doctrine. They are nonfiction argument rather than fiction, but the declared ideological purpose meets revised V5.

The account explains preventable harm through system design and the distribution of risk. Proposals to change those conditions are allowed under revised V5; the earlier broad civic-advocacy rationale is not an explicit manifesto finding.
The retained evidence identifies a declared decolonial restitution manifesto for museums. Scholarship on provenance does not remove this explicit activist purpose; V5 still applies.

The work explicitly presents intervention history as a campaigning anti-imperialist account supporting resistance. That declared ideological and activist purpose meets the revised rule; a critical historical perspective alone would not.

The work argues about employment incentives, meaning and institutional dysfunction, then proposes alternatives. That explanatory critique is not automatically an explicit ideological text; the prior sampling and causal weaknesses stay in the score.

V1 remains on the prior specialist evidence: substantive technical and institutional errors affect the central Operation Paperclip narrative. The revised eligibility and activism rules do not repair the documented reliability problem.

The reported critique of elite philanthropy proposes democratic alternatives. The old record establishes a preferred distribution of reform power but not a sufficiently explicit manifesto or activism declaration; revised V5 allows proposals.

This is an explicitly named communist political manifesto. V5 remains decisive; the existing V1 and V2 concerns about necessary historical victory and allegiance-dependent argument are retained separately.
The work explicitly calls for a movement against mass incarceration and racial caste. This central mobilization purpose meets revised V5 independently of whether its institutional analysis is useful.

The account of settlement and transport develops a preferred urban design. Environmental or civic design proposals are expressly permitted; the earlier veto relied on normative purpose rather than an explicit activist declaration.

V1 remains: the cited specialist critiques identify concrete source-context and chronology errors supporting the book's central failure narrative. The decision does not rely only on an interested CIA response or on political disagreement.

The autobiography explicitly addresses public opinion in support of abolition and political change. That declared civil-activist intervention remains V5, while the historical testimony retains counterfactual value.

The history explicitly advances a reproductive-rights civil campaign rather than only presenting policy possibilities. The retained evidence supports the narrower activist purpose; V5 remains with moderate boundary confidence.

The book explicitly defines and promotes a democratic-liberal political program against rival doctrines. Its declared ideological positioning is central, so V5 remains; centrist status does not itself exempt an ideological text.

The retained work is an explicitly campaigning political polemic against American intervention, rather than solely a comparative foreign-policy account. Its activist purpose supports V5 without a new unsupported V1 or V2 claim.
V4 remains because the central payoff depends on a forecast of globalization's collapse. Geographic and supply-chain observations retain value but do not establish the predicted trajectory.

The history of human concepts of divinity ends with a universal-spirituality proposal. That conclusion does not by itself make the whole a base or derived religious text; revised V5 permits a vision. Existing inferential limits remain.

The book explicitly seeks to persuade religious readers to abandon religion and develops an anti-religious ideological campaign. V5 remains on that declared purpose; atheism as an author's personal view would not suffice.

The theses explicitly articulate Situationist revolutionary doctrine and opposition to capitalist social relations. This is an ideological text under revised V5, beyond an incidental political inclination.

V1 remains: the move from hemispheric asymmetry to a causal history of Western civilization lacks the neurological support identified in the prior specialist critique. The existence of real asymmetries does not establish that bridge.

The work explicitly advances degrowth as a collective political and ecological transformation. Its organizing movement program meets V5, rather than being rejected merely for discussing environmental constraints.
The essay is an explicit anticolonial ideological and emancipatory declaration. Its literary and historical influence do not alter the revised V5 category.

A historical reinterpretation from an Indigenous and decolonial perspective is not automatically an explicit activism declaration. The earlier record principally identifies viewpoint and purpose, which revised V5 no longer treats as sufficient; scoring retains selection limits.

The information-class thesis is explicitly developed to reframe anticapitalist politics and class struggle. That declared ideological project meets revised V5, independently of the uncertainty in its regime classification.
The witness narrative expressly campaigns against the death penalty and seeks changes in public action. That declared civil-activist purpose remains covered by V5; memoir form does not change it.
The work advances a preferred understanding and practice of religion rather than only describing religious history. Its constructive religious teaching is derived religious argument under V5.
The commemorative account explicitly promotes the revolutionary communist legacy as an emancipatory political project. This is a declared ideological text, not simply a history of its influence.
The central argument explicitly calls for ending animal exploitation and rejects reformist ethical-meat alternatives. This movement advocacy meets the narrowed V5 rule.
The memoir and prison testimony expressly ask readers to continue the opposition movement. That explicit political-activism declaration sustains V5; political biography alone would not.

The scholarly work expressly develops Black feminist thought as a program of empowerment, social justice and action. That declared ideological and activist purpose meets V5; scholarly form itself passes revised H2.

The argument connects forms of intelligence and proposes ecological coexistence. A political or environmental vision is expressly allowed; the earlier veto did not establish an explicit manifesto distinct from the explanatory argument.
The history addresses Christians with an explicit religious and antiracist call to change church conduct. Both derived religious exhortation and declared civil activism support V5.

The reporting explicitly seeks a change in readers' participation in animal consumption and advances an animal-welfare cause. This declared activist purpose remains V5, beyond the simple presence of ethical views.
The nominated work is a foundational Daoist teaching text. Secular applications do not change its base religious-text identity under revised V5.

The retained evidence identifies an explicit program to dismantle and rebuild the idea of progress to prevent ecological destruction. The activist declaration remains central enough for V5; the historical subject alone would not.
The dialogue culminates in an endorsed Biblical and Gospel revelation as an explanatory key. That constructive theological teaching supports V5; the mimetic concepts retain counterfactual value.

The memoir interprets American institutions and proposes renewed community and democratic capitalism. A civic vision at its conclusion is allowed by revised V5; the earlier record did not establish an explicit manifesto independent of that vision.

The autobiography explicitly advances and defends a religious-political movement through its participant account. That declared movement purpose remains V5, rather than a veto inferred only from the author's identity.

The historical collection has a civic perspective and a concluding reparations argument. Those features establish a proposal, not automatically an explicit manifesto for the whole work; the prior evidence does not independently establish V1 or V2 for this book.

V1 remains on the cited specialist evidence concerning the central construction of medieval intellectual life and its transformation. The revised H2 and V5 wording does not resolve those historical reliability defects.

The reported history argues for drug-policy change. A policy reform conclusion is expressly permitted; the old broad advocacy finding is insufficient for revised V5. Existing reporting and causal reservations remain in the score.

The retained evidence identifies an explicitly campaigning media argument against consent for the Gaza war. This declared political-activism purpose, rather than its subject or legal vocabulary, sustains V5.

The case studies of private coercion propose a different economic settlement. A normative institutional remedy is allowed; the earlier record supplies no independent serious V2 or explicit manifesto finding.

The history deliberately adopts an oppositional perspective. Revised V5 allows bias and civilizational inclination, and the prior review did not independently establish serious V2. An interpretive history is not automatically a declaration of activism.
The book is an explicit argument for a prison-abolition movement. That central civil and political mobilization meets revised V5.

The publisher identifies the aim of freeing readers from attachment to capitalism to enable political transformation. That explicit anticapitalist ideological purpose goes beyond incidental proposals and sustains V5.
The nominated corpus is religious scripture. Revised V5 expressly retains base religious texts; questions of canon or translation do not alter the gate.

The essays combine botanical knowledge, Indigenous teachings and an ecological ethic. Cultural or spiritual perspective and a proposed relationship with nature do not alone establish a religious text or explicit activist declaration under narrowed V5.

The independent V1 concern remains: the inferential bridge from neuroscience to a comprehensive account of reality exceeds the reviewed support. Its constructive sacred worldview also remains a separately supported religious V5 ground.

The analysis challenges class stereotypes and favors a different class politics. Revised V5 permits that political inclination; the earlier finding did not establish an explicit movement declaration or independent serious ideological capture.

V3 remains: the journals chiefly preserve travel impressions and the author's inner life. The reviewed scope still lacks a sustained transferable mechanism after the particular encounters are removed.
The work expressly advances a Black feminist ideological project and seeks changes in feminist political practice. This declared movement purpose remains covered by V5.

V1 remains: the cited specialist reception identifies a serious national-character causal generalization within the explanation of Nazism. Narrative importance does not remove that independently assessed inferential defect.

V1 remains on the prior criticism of selective historical fragments supporting the central wartime counterfactual. The explicit pacifist intervention also remains a V5 ground; no inference is made that all antiwar arguments are vetoed.

The narrative expressly advances the American Indian Movement and a particular legal-defense campaign. This is supported civil-activist purpose under the revised V5 rule, not merely history about a movement.
V1 remains on the prior assessment of unsupported connections and motives in the central intelligence-conspiracy explanation. The narrower H2 and V5 rules do not repair those causal gaps.
The constitutional polemic explicitly advances a racial-justice political campaign. Its declared activist purpose meets V5; legal analysis or criticism by itself would not.
V3 remains: the family memoir's main payload is personal experience and comic remembrance, with little developed reusable explanatory structure. Neither revised rule addresses that limitation.
The lectures directly teach Buddhist spiritual understanding and liberation. This is derived religious teaching under V5, even where individual observations about self-deception have secular use.
V1 remains: treating cultures as organisms with necessary life stages is an unsupported causal scheme in the reviewed evidence. Resemblances and later events do not establish its deterministic model.

The year-long household narrative investigates food production and consumption while proposing a different way of life. That personal environmental vision is allowed by revised V5; the older record inferred activism from advocacy alone.

The personal letter interprets racial experience and American social order. An interpretive stance is not an explicit activist declaration; revised V5 does not exclude a memoir solely for civil or political meaning. Existing low domain fit remains.
The talks directly teach spiritual awakening and liberation from attachment. This is derived religious-spiritual teaching under V5, rather than merely a memoir with religious experiences.
V1 remains on the cited economic-historical criticism of the central coercion-to-productivity inference and quantitative handling. The thematic subject is separate from that evidential finding.
The work is an explicit tenant-movement manifesto for abolishing rent-based domination. Revised V5 directly retains this category.

The essays analyze the attention economy and propose redirected attention and local engagement. Such a civic and ecological vision is allowed; the earlier broad advocacy rationale does not establish a separate explicit manifesto.

V1 remains: the prior specialist critique identifies selective primate comparisons and neglected pair-bond and forager evidence central to the thesis. Revised H2 and V5 do not resolve that inferential failure.
